title: Ops: Opsctl admin utilities + runbooks-as-tasks integration for support workflows
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a safe, auditable admin utility (opsctl) plus a runbooks-as-tasks system so Support/Oncall can execute common remediation flows without engineering intervention. This ticket tracks the end-to-end integration: CLI/Service, Slack shortcuts, automatic Linear task creation from runbook steps, and audit/event export to our KMS-backed log store.

Scope:
- opsctl: a scoped admin CLI and accompanying HTTP service that issues short-lived action tokens and enforces RBAC per role.
- runbooks-as-tasks: author runbooks in markdown (Confluence/Git) that can be executed as a Linear task, with explicit checkpoints, required approvals, and automatic result capture.
- Support automation: Slack actions + a lightweight web UI for Support to launch runbook tasks; generated Linear tasks are pinned to the relevant customer and surface links back to ticketing (Zendesk) and observability dashboards.

Out of scope for this ticket: full SSO onboarding for external contractors, custom workflow templating (follow-up ticket planned).
acceptance_criteria:
1) opsctl can perform read and safe write actions (cache purge, scaledown, config toggle) only when invoked with a valid team role and logged audit entry is produced.
2) Authoring a runbook in Confluence with YAML metadata launches a Linear task via webhook when a support agent presses the Slack shortcut.
3) Linear task contains structured fields: runbook id, step checklist, links to PR/dashboards/Zendesk, and a populated execution log after run completes.
4) No plaintext secrets in logs; all tokens encrypted at rest and traceable to invoking principal.
5) Smoke tests pass in staging and a canary cohort of 3 support agents successfully resolve test incidents using the flow.
implementation_notes:
High level plan:
- Phase A: opsctl API + token broker (short-lived) + basic RBAC mapping to SSO groups. Minimal CLI for engineers.
- Phase B: Runbook runner service that translates a markdown runbook into an executable checklist. Each checklist step maps to an opsctl action or a manual confirmation.
- Phase C: Slack action + Linear integration: Slack invokes runbook-runner API, which creates a Linear task (ENG-prefixed) with checklist items. Completion updates Linear and posts results back to Slack and Zendesk.

Key tech choices: reuse our existing token/iam library, store runbook metadata in Confluence and cache parsed versions in Redis, persist execution events to clickhouse/audit-store. Use existing Linear API wrapper library for task creation.

PR references: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-admin/pull/58 (opsctl prototype), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbook-runner/pull/12
risks:
- Privilege escalation if RBAC mapping is incomplete. Mitigation: require manager approval for high-risk actions and add a safe-mode toggle that blocks destructive actions in canary.
- Mis-typed runbooks could run harmful sequences. Mitigation: validation on authoring (linting) and step-level dry-run support.
- Audit volume growth affecting storage costs. Mitigation: sampling policy and TTL on detailed step logs, with full exports for incidents only.
qa_steps:
1) Create staging runbook with 3 steps: read-only monitor query, cache purge (safe), record outcome.
2) From Slack staging workspace, trigger runbook via shortcut and confirm Linear task is created and assigned to the invoking user.
3) Run through steps in task UI; verify opsctl actions execute in staging and entries appear in audit-store.
4) Verify tokens expire and cannot be reused after TTL.
5) Confirm no secrets are present in Linear task body or in Slack thread.
